maria (eng-platform): quick idea — can we add a lightweight request header to opt a token into v1 compatibility for a bounded rollout?

josh (eng-runtime): curious, what's the intended semantics? full v1 behavior or only routing fallback?

maria (eng-platform): routing + quota treatment. think of it as a temporary shim: if header present -> route through v1 compatibility path and apply legacy quota rules. we then collect diffs.

sara (console-ux): we'd need a console affordance. show a per-token 'compat opt-in' toggle and a small risk meter if they opt into legacy routing.

maria (eng-platform): exactly. we can sample 1% by default and let customer request opt-in. backend flag: x-compat-mode: v1

josh (eng-runtime): technically easy: add header check in routing layer. pseudocode:```python
mode = req.headers.get('x-compat-mode')
if mode == 'v1':
    route = route_to_v1_fallback(req)
else:
    route = route_to_v2(req)
```

josh (eng-runtime): caveat: KV cache and batching semantics differ — need isolation so v1-routed requests don't steal v2's cache.

kevin (eng-sre): important: quotas. If we treat compat-routed as legacy quota, we must avoid double-billing tokens when we also sample for telemetry. Define a single source of truth for usage attribution.

maria (eng-platform): proposal: compat header sets a routing tag `compat:v1` in request metadata. billing pipeline reads tag and applies legacy price-plan if customer is on legacy plan. sampling/probes should set `probe:true` not to mutate billing.

sara (console-ux): UI note: show a tiny inline badge "compat" next to routes/keys that have ever seen compat traffic; clicking opens a timeline with sampling% and error divergence.

josh (eng-runtime): telemetry: we'll emit a delta metric per request: `response_model_version` and `response_diff_hash` when probe=true. That lets us signal regressions without storing full payloads.

kevin (eng-sre): add an alert: if divergence rate > 2% and median latency regress > 50ms for a tenant with >100qps, page oncall.

maria (eng-platform): ops fallback: if v2 capacity constrained, we already fallback to compatible variants. we should avoid automatic routing purely because header is present — header only overrides normal routing when customer explicitly requests. default behavior unchanged.

sara (console-ux): mockup incoming: small toggle in API keys view: [ ] Enable compatibility opt-in (beta) — when enabled, show sampling slider + estimated cost delta. Need an endpoint to preview the 'compat risk score' for a key.

josh (eng-runtime): can implement `POST /keys/:id/compat-preview` that returns {sample_rate, estimated_qps_impact, risk_score}. We'll need a stable risk calc.

kevin (eng-sre): telemetry payload shape proposal: `tenant, key_id, compat_tag, probe, response_diff_hash, latency_ms, model_variant` — minimal, no PII. store as timeseries.

maria (eng-platform): rollout plan sketch: 1) infra flag + header parsing + tagging 2) telemetry emit + console preview 3) 1% sampling + invite a few customers 4) increase sampling and enable opt-in toggle 5) GA if safe.

sara (console-ux): question: how do we surface customers that would benefit most? maybe compute a 'compat-need' score from request logs (old clients that send v1 payload shapes).

josh (eng-runtime): we can approximate by checking requests that previously got fallthrough routes and measuring the frequency. low-effort heuristic.

infra-bot: deploy queued: runtime/compat-header-check -> canary on prod-edge in 5m :rocket:

maria (eng-platform): thanks — I'll draft a short RFC and a console mock. keeping sampling conservative so we don't touch billing unexpectedly.

kevin (eng-sre): +1. I'll add the alert rules and retention plan for the diff hashes (30 days).

sara (console-ux): I'll attach mock screenshots to the RFC.

josh (eng-runtime): will open a PR for header parsing + tag plumbing, link in thread.

maria (eng-platform): awesome. tagging followups: @josh for runtime PR, @sara for UI, @kevin for alerts/billing validation. we'll sync tomorrow at 11am. :thumbsup:
